replies.author: de0u
replies.text:
cdflasdkesalkjfkdfkjsdajfd I was wondering if it’s possible for something to be installed on my phone that would survive a wipe—even if the bootloader is locked—should the device be out of my sight for a few minutes.

If the bootloader is locked then the system partition is checked against the signing key (either Google's, or else the signing key with the hash that the bootloader displays) every time the device boots.

Some of the checking is lazy, so it is hypothetically possible to make a change that would be discovered only after booting starts, but before the changed content could be read dm-verity would trip a corruption alert.

The Android Verified Boot infrastructure is explicitly designed to detect and report changes to the system partition.

Users concerned about esoteric threats such as a fake or obsolete bootloader may wish to use Auditor.
